subChunks.title: COALESCE, NULLIF, and IFNULL
subChunks.hookHtml: NULLs require special handling in almost every non-trivial query. Three functions — COALESCE, NULLIF, and IFNULL — cover the most common patterns.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
COALESCE — first non-NULL wins

COALESCE(a, b, c)  -- returns first non-NULL of a, b, c

SELECT name, COALESCE(mentor_id, -1) AS mentor
FROM apprentices;  -- -1 where mentor_id is NULL

SELECT COALESCE(description, short_desc, 'No description') FROM items;

Takes any number of arguments. Evaluates left-to-right and returns the first non-NULL. The standard way to substitute defaults for NULL.

NULLIF — produce NULL when equal

NULLIF(a, b)  -- returns NULL if a = b, else returns a

-- Avoid division by zero:
SELECT total / NULLIF(count, 0) AS avg FROM stats;
-- If count = 0, NULLIF returns NULL; NULL/anything = NULL (not error)

Classic use case: protect against division by zero. If the denominator equals the sentinel value (0, 'N/A', etc.), return NULL instead of crashing.

IFNULL (MySQL/SQLite) / ISNULL (SQL Server)

IFNULL(a, fallback)  -- same as COALESCE(a, fallback)
SELECT IFNULL(mentor_id, 0) FROM apprentices;

Two-argument shorthand for COALESCE. Not in the SQL standard — prefer COALESCE for portability.

NVL (Oracle)

Oracle uses NVL(a, b) for the same purpose. Not covered further — all modern-Oracle queries should use COALESCE.

storyBeats.text: The XP leaderboard crashes — division by zero. A count column was zero for one apprentice.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: COALESCE provides defaults for missing values — first non-NULL wins. NULLIF inverts this: it converts a specific value into NULL, which is most useful for turning zeros into NULLs before division. Together, they handle the overwhelming majority of NULL-related problems.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 Safe defaults

Return name and COALESCE(mentor_id, 0) AS mentor_id for all apprentices. Also return NULLIF(xp, 0) AS xp_or_null to replace zero XP with NULL.
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
SELECT
  name,
  COALESCE(mentor_id, 0)  AS mentor_id,
  NULLIF(xp, 0)           AS xp_or_null
FROM apprentices;

guidedPracticeTests.label: Returns 6 rows
guidedPracticeTests.setup: CREATE TABLE apprentices (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, rank TEXT NOT NULL, xp INTEGER NOT NULL, mentor_id INTEGER); INSERT INTO apprentices VALUES (1,'Alice','Apprentice',1200,1),(2,'Bjorn','Adept',2400,2),(3,'Cassia','Mage',4800,1),(4,'Dorian','Novice',80,NULL),(5,'Elara','Archmage',7500,3),(6,'Fenrir','Apprentice',950,NULL);

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml:
🏹 Solo

Write a query that computes total_score / NULLIF(attempts, 0) AS avg_score for each apprentice from a hypothetical stats(apprentice_id, total_score, attempts) table. Use COALESCE to return 0 when avg_score would be NULL.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain COALESCE and NULLIF in plain language. Give a concrete example of why NULLIF is useful for division.

questions.explanation: COALESCE evaluates left to right and returns the first non-NULL. Both first arguments are NULL, so it reaches 'default' and returns it.
NULLIF(a, b) returns NULL when a equals b. When count = 0, NULLIF returns NULL. This is used before division: total / NULLIF(count, 0) returns NULL instead of a division-by-zero error.

questions.prompt: What is the portable SQL equivalent of IFNULL(col, 'default')?
questions.explanation: COALESCE is the SQL standard function for this pattern. IFNULL (MySQL/SQLite), NVL (Oracle), and ISNULL (SQL Server) are engine-specific. COALESCE works across all major engines.

questions.prompt: Why might `SELECT AVG(COALESCE(score, 0)) FROM completions` give a different answer than `SELECT AVG(score) FROM completions`?
options: COALESCE replaces NULLs with 0 before averaging — adding zeros increases the count of values and lowers the average; AVG(score) ignores NULLs entirely
They always return the same result
COALESCE(score, 0) does not compile inside AVG
questions.answer: COALESCE replaces NULLs with 0 before averaging — adding zeros increases the count of values and lowers the average; AVG(score) ignores NULLs entirely
questions.explanation: AVG(score) computes the average over non-NULL values only. AVG(COALESCE(score, 0)) includes the NULL-replaced-by-zero rows in both the sum and the count, pulling the average lower. Choose based on whether NULLs mean 'unknown' (use AVG) or 'zero' (use COALESCE first).
